comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that Δtgt shows specific tobramycin sensitivity. OpenEval emphasizes competition and survival assays (C1, C29, C47-C50), while peer review also includes the membrane potential/uptake findings (C51-C52). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with high confidence.

OpenEval R2 addresses membrane potential and uptake controls (C51-C52) that peer review R1 includes in their acceptance of the core tobramycin phenotype. Both agree these controls rule out alternative mechanisms.

Perfect overlap on codon-specific decoding claims (C3, C40, C60-C66). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly confirms 'Q is essential for the efficient translation of TAT codons' and OpenEval notes the GFP reporter data clearly demonstrates differential codon effects.

Both address tRNA overexpression rescue experiments (C55-C57, C67-C68). OpenEval R3 is SUPPORTED and includes additional claims about tRNA levels (C53-C54). Peer review R3 accepts these findings as part of the molecular reporter approach without specific critique.

OpenEval R3 includes control data on unchanged tRNA levels (C53-C54) that peer review R15 accepts as supporting the interpretation that effects are due to modification rather than tRNA abundance changes.
OpenEval R6 addresses tRNA overexpression effects on decoding (C67-C72), overlapping with peer review R3's acceptance of rescue experiments (C55-C57, C67-C68). Both are SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on β-lactamase reporter validation (C73-C79). OpenEval notes this provides biologically relevant validation of GFP findings. Peer review confirms experiments are 'well-designed and conducted.' Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect overlap on decoding fidelity and mistranslation claims (C80-C86). Both SUPPORTED. Peer review specifically mentions this section was added after reviewer suggestion and approves the findings on stop codon readthrough and near-cognate decoding.

Both address proteomics identification of RsxA and codon usage analysis (C4, C87-C89, C91-C92). OpenEval is SUPPORTED. Peer review confirms 'absence of Q increases rsxA translation, because rsxA gene has a high TAT codon bias.'
OpenEval R9 includes proteomics and codon usage analysis (C87-C88) that peer review R16 accepts as part of the methodology supporting the insufficient proteomics conclusion.

Major disagreement on ribosome profiling interpretation (C95-C99). OpenEval is SUPPORTED, but peer review is UNCERTAIN, stating 'the interpretation of the results of RiboSeq data carried out in this work remains controversial' and requesting comparison with proteomics data.

OpenEval R10 acknowledges proteomics limitations (C93-C94), which peer review R16 implicitly validates by noting the complexity of relating proteomics to translation efficiency in their RiboSeq concerns.

Both address RsxA translational regulation (C5-C6, C41-C42, C105-C116 in OpenEval; C5-C6, C41, C114-C115 in peer review). Both SUPPORTED. Peer review confirms 'increased RsxA in the absence of Q inhibits SoxR response.'
OpenEval R11 includes GFP fusion reporter data (C107-C113) that peer review R7 accepts as part of the molecular reporter approach supporting the RsxA mechanism. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on RsxA toxicity and functional validation (C117-C120). OpenEval is SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts this as part of the mechanism discovery using 'a variety of strains, assays, and advanced techniques.'

Both address E. coli validation experiments (C128-C129) demonstrating species-specific differences. OpenEval is SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts these comparative findings as demonstrating generalizability while acknowledging species specificity.

Both address tgt regulation under stress (C132-C134). OpenEval is SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts this as part of the overall mechanism whereby 'changes in Q modification levels control the decoding of mRNAs enriched in TAT codons under antibiotic stress.'

Both address Q34 modification measurements (C143, C150-C153, C202). OpenEval is SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts the use of 'advanced proteomics' and mass spectrometry as part of the technical approach supporting dynamic Q34 regulation.

Partial disagreement on UV damage mechanism (C8, C45, C154-C160, C190). OpenEval is SUPPORTED based on GO enrichment and phenotypic validation. Peer review is UNCERTAIN, stating 'the phenotype is striking, but the mechanism remains somewhat unclear' and future work is needed.

Strong agreement on species-specific codon bias patterns (C161-C162, C164-C165). Both SUPPORTED. Peer review notes the manuscript 'improves our understanding' and accepts the comparative analysis demonstrating species specificity.

Strong agreement on the integrated model of Q34-mediated translational control (C7, C43-C44, C167-C169). Both SUPPORTED. Peer review confirms the model where 'Tgt serves as a molecular pivot point to reprogram translational output in response to stress.'

Both address organism-specific effects and comparison with literature (C173-C178). Both SUPPORTED. Peer review notes the work is 'very complete and interesting' and accepts the comparative analysis across organisms.

Strong agreement on the MoTT framework and generalizability (C187-C190, C206-C207). OpenEval is SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly endorses the work as improving 'understanding of Modification Tunable Transcripts' and being 'useful for the field.'

OpenEval R4 addresses established background knowledge about Tgt function and wobble base pairing (C2, C30-C32). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this represents contextual information rather than experimental findings requiring peer validation.

OpenEval R20 marks speculative claims about factors influencing observed effects (C185-C186, C241-C243, C245-C247, C251) as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation; these represent future research directions not specifically addressed by reviewers.

OpenEval R22 addresses codon usage optimization principles (C191-C195) as SUPPORTED by analysis and literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation; this represents interpretive framework accepted without specific comment.

OpenEval R23 addresses tgt regulation mechanisms and Q34 dynamics (C196-C205) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviews R10 and R11 partially overlap on regulation (C201-C202) but don't comprehensively evaluate all mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval R24 marks broader evolutionary and regulatory implications (C208-C210, C219, C222, C224-C227, C233) as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation; these represent speculative hypotheses for future investigation not specifically addressed by reviewers.
